### CookieOptions

Interface. `import type { CookieOptions } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface CookieOptions {
    maxAge?: number;
    expires?: Date | string;
    path?: string;
    domain?: string;
    httpOnly?: boolean;
    secure?: boolean;
    sameSite?: "Lax" | "Strict" | "None" | "lax" | "strict" | "none";
}
```

Options for `ctx.setCookie` / `ctx.deleteCookie`.

Members:

- `maxAge`: Lifetime in seconds (`Max-Age`).
- `expires`: `Expires`: a Date, or a string sent as written.
- `path`: Defaults to "/".
- `domain`: `Domain`. Not sent by default (the cookie stays on the request's host).
- `httpOnly`: Defaults to true. Set to false explicitly to drop HttpOnly.
- `secure`: `Secure`. Defaults to false.
- `sameSite`: Defaults to "Lax".

Used by: [`LoaderContext`](#loadercontext).

### Session

Interface. `import type { Session } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface Session {
    readonly readOnly: boolean;
    get<T = unknown>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>;
    has(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
    set(key: string, value: unknown): Promise<void>;
    delete(key: string): Promise<void>;
    regenerate(): Promise<void>;
    destroy(): Promise<void>;
}
```

`ctx.session` (and `getContext().session`): per-visitor values kept across requests in an
encrypted cookie (or, with a `store` in session.ts, server-side behind a signed id). Values must
be JSON. Created on first access; reading it makes an ISR page per-user. Needs
`NOWAKI_SESSION_SECRET` in production (dev generates one into `.nowaki/session-secret`).

Members:

- `readOnly`: True where the session can't be changed: on a cross-site request that changes state (it is
  also empty there, CSRF) unless the route exports `csrf = false`, and in live island renders.
  Writes throw there.
- `get`: The value of `key`, or undefined.
- `has`: Whether `key` is set.
- `set`: Sets a JSON value (`undefined` deletes). Without a `store`, throws when the cookie would pass
  4 KB. Throws after the response headers were sent (a `streaming = "early"` page's loaders).
- `delete`: Removes `key`.
- `regenerate`: A fresh cookie (and, with a store, a new id), keeping the values. Call it on sign-in.
- `destroy`: Clears the values and the cookie. Call it on sign-out.

Used by: [`LoaderContext`](#loadercontext).

### LoaderContext

Interface. `import type { LoaderContext } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface LoaderContext {
    readonly url: URL;
    readonly routePath: string;
    readonly site: URL | undefined;
    readonly params: RouteParams;
    readonly method: string;
    readonly locale: string | undefined;
    readonly headers: Record<string, string>;
    readonly cookies: Record<string, string>;
    readonly session: Session;
    readonly req?: unknown;
    state: Record<string, unknown>;
    actionData?: unknown;
    get(name: string): string | undefined;
    formData(): Promise<FormData>;
    bodyText(): Promise<string>;
    bodyJson<T = unknown>(): Promise<T>;
    status(code: number): this;
    setHeader(name: string, value: string): this;
    setCookie(name: string, value: string, opts?: CookieOptions): this;
    deleteCookie(name: string, opts?: CookieOptions): this;
    redirect(to: string, status?: number, opts?: {
        basePath?: boolean;
    }): NowakiResult;
    redirect(to: string, opts: {
        basePath?: boolean;
    }): NowakiResult;
    json<T>(data: T, init?: ResponseInit): NowakiResult;
    html(markup: string, init?: ResponseInit): NowakiResult;
    text(s: string, init?: ResponseInit): NowakiResult;
}
```

Shared context passed to loaders, actions, middleware, and API handlers.
Bundles the request (url, params, method, headers, cookies, body) and
response writers (status, header, cookie, redirect, json, ...).

Members:

- `url`: The request URL, as the browser sent it (basePath and locale prefix included).
- `routePath`: The route path: `url.pathname` without nowaki.config `basePath` and without the
  locale prefix (`/gallery/ja/photo/1` → `/photo/1`), the form `<Link href>`, `href()` and
  `revalidatePath()` take. After a config rewrite, it is the rewritten path. In components, use
  `routePath(url)` from `@nowaki-dev/runtime/navigation`.
- `site`: The site's URL (`NOWAKI_SITE`, or `site` in nowaki.config), for absolute links in feeds and
  the like. Undefined when neither is set; `url.origin` is the request's own origin.
- `params`: Route params (catch-all values are arrays).
- `method`: The HTTP method.
- `locale`: The request's locale with `i18n` in nowaki.config: the locale prefix of the URL (`/ja/about`
  → `"ja"`), else the default locale. Undefined without i18n and for `/__nowaki/*` requests
  (server functions, live events).
- `headers`: Request headers (lowercase keys).
- `cookies`: Parsed request cookies.
- `session`: The visitor's session (see [`Session`](#session)). Throws on first access in production when
  `NOWAKI_SESSION_SECRET` is missing, and while prerendering.

  Example:

  ```tsx
  await ctx.session.regenerate(); // on sign-in
  await ctx.session.set("userId", user.id);
  ```
- `req`: Node's `IncomingMessage` where there is one (undefined on the edge adapters). Not covered by
  semver. Reading it makes an ISR page uncacheable.
- `state`: Arbitrary data middleware passes to loaders and pages.
- `actionData`: The action's return value (passed when the page re-renders).
- `get`: Gets a request header (case-insensitive).
- `formData`: Reads the request body as `FormData` for both `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and
  `multipart/form-data` (same as the platform `Request.formData()`). Text fields are strings;
  file parts are `File`. `form.get()` is `string | File | null` — read text with
  `String(form.get("x") ?? "")`. Oversized or malformed bodies throw before user code runs
  (413/400). **`File.name` is untrusted** (may contain CR/LF or `../`) — sanitize before
  storage or display.
- `bodyText`: Reads the request body as a string.
- `bodyJson`: Reads the request body as JSON (`null` for an empty body).
- `status`: Sets the response status (chainable).
- `setHeader`: Sets a response header (chainable).
- `setCookie`: Appends a Set-Cookie header (chainable).
- `deleteCookie`: Deletes a cookie (Max-Age=0, chainable).
- `redirect`: Redirects (302 by default). Return it from a loader, action, or middleware. Under
  nowaki.config `basePath`, a path starting with `/` gets the base in front unless it already
  starts with it; `{ basePath: false }` sends `to` as written.
- `json`: Returns a JSON response.
- `html`: Returns an HTML response.
- `text`: Returns a text/plain response.

Uses: [`RouteParams`](#routeparams), [`Session`](#session), [`CookieOptions`](#cookieoptions), [`NowakiResult`](#nowakiresult), [`ResponseInit`](#responseinit).

Used by: [`Loader`](#loader), [`Action`](#action), [`ApiHandler`](#apihandler), [`Middleware`](#middleware), [`getContext`](#getcontext).

### StaticPaths

Type. `import type { StaticPaths } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type StaticPaths<P extends RouteParams = RouteParams> = P[] | ((info: {
    locale?: string;
}) => P[] | Promise<P[]>);
```

`export const staticPaths` on a dynamic route: the params to prerender with `nowaki prerender`
or the static adapter, one page per entry. A `[...rest]` param takes a string[]. With i18n, a
function runs once per locale, given `{ locale }` (also `getLocale()`, so `getCollection` returns
that locale's entries), and each page is written under the locale's prefix.

Example:

```tsx
export const staticPaths: StaticPaths = [{ slug: "hello" }, { slug: "world" }];
```

Uses: [`RouteParams`](#routeparams).

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule), [`ApiModule`](#apimodule).

### RouteBudget

Type. `import type { RouteBudget } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type RouteBudget = {
    js: number;
};
```

`export const budget` on a page route: the most first-load client JS the page may ship, in KB of
gzip (the islands runtime, the islands it can render, and the live runtime). `nowaki build`
fails when the page goes over it. `js` must be a number literal; `0` means no client JS.

Example:

```tsx
export const budget = { js: 12 };
```

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule).

### Streaming

Type. `import type { Streaming } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type Streaming = boolean | "early";
```

`export const streaming` on a page route.
- `true`: the loaders run first, then the shell is sent and the body streams as it renders
  (Suspense boundaries arrive as they settle). A loader redirect or error still sets the status.
- `"early"`: the shell is sent before any loader runs, so the first byte doesn't wait for data.
  The status and headers are then fixed: `meta` sees only the static `title` / `head`, a loader
  redirect becomes a client-side `location.replace`, and a loader error renders the nearest
  `error.tsx` in the page (its message only in dev). Cookies set by a loader are not sent.

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule).

### Csrf

Type. `import type { Csrf } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type Csrf = boolean;
```

`export const csrf` on a page with an `action`, an API route (`routes/api/**`), or a file route
(`feed.xml.ts`). By default (`true`, so exporting `true` changes nothing) a POST / PUT / PATCH /
DELETE from another site is rejected with 403 `Forbidden` before the action or handler runs: an
`Origin` of another host or `null`, or `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` without `Origin`. Requests
without either header (curl, server-to-server, most native apps) and GET / HEAD / OPTIONS are
never checked. `_middleware` runs before the check.

`false` accepts cross-site writes, for webhooks and third-party callbacks. Authenticate such a
route another way (a signature header, a shared secret): its cookies are the visitor's.

Example:

```tsx
export const csrf = false; // routes/api/webhook.ts
```

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule), [`ApiModule`](#apimodule).

### DocumentAttrs

Type. `import type { DocumentAttrs } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type DocumentAttrs = Record<string, string | number | boolean | null | undefined>;
```

Attributes for `<html>` / `<body>` (`export const htmlAttrs` / `bodyAttrs` in a route or
layout, or from `meta()`). Layouts apply first, then the route, then `meta()`; a later value
wins, `false` / `null` removes one set earlier, and `class` values are joined. `true` renders
a bare attribute. Event-handler attributes (`on*`) are ignored.

Used by: [`Meta`](#meta), [`PageModule`](#pagemodule), [`LayoutModule`](#layoutmodule).

### Meta

Interface. `import type { Meta } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface Meta {
    title?: string;
    head?: string;
    lang?: string;
    htmlAttrs?: DocumentAttrs;
    bodyAttrs?: DocumentAttrs;
    description?: string;
    canonical?: string | true;
    robots?: string | {
        index?: boolean;
        follow?: boolean;
    };
    openGraph?: {
        title?: string;
        description?: string;
        type?: string;
        url?: string;
        siteName?: string;
        locale?: string;
        image?: OpenGraphImage | OpenGraphImage[];
    };
    twitter?: {
        card?: "summary" | "summary_large_image" | "app" | "player";
        site?: string;
        creator?: string;
        title?: string;
        description?: string;
        image?: string;
        imageAlt?: string;
    };
    jsonLd?: Record<string, unknown> | Record<string, unknown>[];
}
```

Page metadata (`<title>` / `<head>` / `<html lang>` / `<html>` and `<body>` attributes).

Members:

- `title`: `<title>`.
- `head`: Raw HTML put in `<head>` as written (no escaping: never build it from user input).
- `lang`: `<html lang>`.
- `htmlAttrs`: Attributes for `<html>` (see [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs)).
- `bodyAttrs`: Attributes for `<body>` (see [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs)).
- `description`: `<meta name="description">`; Open Graph and Twitter fall back to it.
- `canonical`: `<link rel="canonical">`: a URL or path (against the site), or `true` for this page's path.
- `robots`: `<meta name="robots">`. A noindex page is left out of the generated sitemap.xml.
- `openGraph`: Open Graph. `title` / `description` default to the page's; `url` to this page; relative URLs resolve against the site.
- `twitter`: Twitter / X cards. `card` defaults to "summary_large_image"; the rest fall back to Open Graph.
- `twitter.imageAlt`: Defaults to the Open Graph image's `alt`.
- `jsonLd`: Structured data, one `<script type="application/ld+json">` per object.

Uses: [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs), [`OpenGraphImage`](#opengraphimage).

Used by: [`MetaFn`](#metafn), [`PageModule`](#pagemodule), [`LayoutModule`](#layoutmodule).

### LayoutProps

Interface. `import type { LayoutProps } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface LayoutProps<D = unknown> {
    data: D;
    params: RouteParams;
    url: URL;
    children: ComponentChildren;
    slots: Record<string, ComponentChildren>;
}
```

Props a `_layout` component receives.

Members:

- `data`: The layout's loader return value.
- `params`: Route params of the page being rendered.
- `url`: The request URL.
- `children`: The page (or the next layout down).
- `slots`: Parallel routes: what each slot directory next to this layout (`@modal/` → `slots.modal`)
  renders, wrapped in `<nowaki-slot name="modal" style="display:contents">`. That's the slot's
  file matching the URL (`@modal/photo/[id].tsx` for `/photo/42`), else its `default.tsx`, else
  null. Slot files get `{ data, params, url }` like a page, and their loaders get the slot's
  params. They don't contribute `meta`.

  Intercepting routes: a file in a slot whose path has a `(.)` / `(..)` / `(...)` segment
  (`@modal/(.)photo/[id].tsx`) takes over that URL on client navigation from a page the slot is
  on: the router fetches just that file and swaps it into the slot (the URL changes, the rest of
  the page and its island state stay; back restores the slot). A reload or a direct visit
  renders the full page. Such a slot is always rendered as its `<nowaki-slot>` element, empty
  when it has nothing to show, so render `slots.modal` even then: it's where the fragment goes.

Uses: [`RouteParams`](#routeparams).

Used by: [`LayoutModule`](#layoutmodule).

### LoadingComponent

Type. `import type { LoadingComponent } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type LoadingComponent = () => unknown;
```

Default export of `routes/loading.tsx`. When a client navigation takes over 150ms,
the nearest loading boundary (nestable) is shown until the target HTML arrives. No island needed.

### ErrorPageProps

Interface. `import type { ErrorPageProps } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface ErrorPageProps {
    error: {
        message: string;
    };
    reset: () => void;
}
```

Props received by the default export of `routes/error.tsx`. When a client navigation fails,
the nearest error boundary (nestable) is shown. The client router puts the message into the
element marked `data-nowaki-error` and wires retry to the element marked `data-nowaki-reset`.

Members:

- `error`: The failure; `message` is what the router puts into `data-nowaki-error`.
- `reset`: Retries the navigation.

### Live

Interface. `import type { Live } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface Live<S = any> {
    state: (props?: any) => S;
    on: Record<string, (state: S, payload?: any) => S | Promise<S>>;
    authorize?: (event: {
        name: string;
        handler: string;
        state: S;
        payload?: any;
    }) => boolean | Promise<boolean>;
    subscribe?: string[] | ((state: S) => string[]);
    load?: (state: S, info: {
        topic: string;
    }) => S | Promise<S>;
    room?: (props: any) => string;
    shared?: (props?: any) => S;
}
```

`export const live` in an island module: a live island (Jetstream). No component JS is sent to
the browser: the server holds the state and sends HTML patches.

Members:

- `state`: The initial state, from the island's props.
- `on`: Event handlers by name (`data-live="name"`), each returning the new state.
- `authorize`: Runs after the state signature is verified and before each handler; anything but `true`
  refuses the event (the client gets `{ type: "error", reason: "forbidden" }`). `getContext()`
  returns the WebSocket upgrade's cookies and headers here and in handlers.
- `subscribe`: Live query topics (or a function of the state): `publish(topic)` refreshes these islands.
- `load`: Runs on `publish(topic)` for a subscribed island; returns the new state to push.
- `room`: Makes this a room island: every instance with the same room id (1-120 characters, no
  whitespace) shares one state, `shared()`. Handlers then receive and return the shared state,
  and every member gets the new HTML. Held in the server process's memory (`nowaki dev` /
  `nowaki start`); not shared across instances. `nowaki start` saves rooms to
  `.nowaki/live-rooms.json` (at most every 2 s, and on SIGTERM / SIGINT) and loads them back on
  the next start (`NOWAKI_LIVE_ROOMS_FILE` picks the file, `off` disables it); under `nowaki dev`
  they are lost on restart.
- `shared`: Initial shared state of a room (`live.room`).

Used by: [`IslandModule`](#islandmodule).

### publish

Function. `import { publish } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export function publish(topic: string): void;
```

Refreshes every live island subscribed to `topic` (`live.subscribe`) by running its `live.load`
and pushing the patch. Call it from actions, server functions, or API routes after data changes.
It reaches the live connections of the same `nowaki dev` / `nowaki start` process. On the deploy
adapters (node, bun, deno, cloudflare, vercel) it does nothing and warns once. A topic is 1 to
128 characters without whitespace (else a TypeError).

### RouteTags

Type. `import type { RouteTags } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type RouteTags = string[] | ((info: {
    params: RouteParams;
    data: any;
}) => string[]);
```

`export const tags` on an ISR page (one with `export const revalidate`): the cache tags its
cached copies carry, so `revalidateTag(tag)` can purge them. An array, or a function of the
render's `{ params, data }` returning one. A tag is 1 to 256 characters without whitespace,
commas or control characters; at most 64 per page (invalid ones are dropped with a warning).
Pages with `streaming = "early"` are never cached, so their tags are unused.

Example:

```tsx
export const tags = ({ params }) => ["posts", `post:${params.slug}`];
```

Uses: [`RouteParams`](#routeparams).

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule).

### revalidatePath

Function. `import { revalidatePath } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export function revalidatePath(path: string): void;
```

Purges every cached copy of the page at `path` from the ISR cache, so the next request renders
it fresh (and waits for that render). `path` is a route path, as written in `<Link href>`: without
the basePath or a locale prefix. Every form a browser can cache it under is purged: each query
string and `Vary` variant, each locale, the basePath, and both trailing-slash forms under
`trailingSlash: "ignore"`. A rewritten URL is cached under the browser's path; use a tag for it.

Call it from a page `action`, an API route, a server function or a live handler after data
changes: under `nowaki start` the purge happens before that response is sent, so a redirect
after the action already shows fresh content. Calls made outside a request, or after its
response was sent (a timer, a queue consumer), reach the cache shortly after. The ISR cache
lives in each `nowaki start` process; with several instances, fan the purge out with
`POST /__nowaki/revalidate` (see `revalidateTag`). Throws a TypeError for a path that isn't
root-relative (`/blog`) or is over 2048 characters.

Per server:

| Server | Cached by | Purge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nowaki start` | the Rust front, in memory per process | deleted before the response is sent |
| vercel adapter | Vercel's CDN (ISR pages send `Vercel-Cache-Tag`) | `dangerouslyDeleteByTag` from `@vercel/functions`, awaited up to 2 s before the response; install the package in the app (warned once without it) |
| node / bun / deno adapters | whatever CDN is in front (`s-maxage`) | none: a no-op, warned once; purge that CDN through its API |
| cloudflare adapter | the Worker, in the Cache API of each data center (custom domains) | the path is deleted from the local data center's cache; with `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Cache Purge permission) set on the Worker, a zone purge by tag clears every data center, awaited up to 2 s; without them (or on workers.dev, which has no zone) `revalidateTag` clears nothing, warned once |
| static output | files | none: a no-op, warned once |
| `nowaki dev` | nothing | calls are only recorded |

On Vercel the path is a cache tag too (`p:<browser path>`, next to `t:<tag>`), so both functions
purge by tag; a tag over 256 bytes is sent as a hash. Make the call inside the request:
`@vercel/functions` purges through the invocation's context, so a call with no request behind
it does nothing, and one made after the response may be cut short when the function suspends.
On Cloudflare the tags go in `Cache-Tag` (a tag over 240 characters is sent as a hash; tags
are case-insensitive there, so a purge can catch more than asked). The zone purge API is rate
limited per account (on the Free plan 5 requests a minute, bursts of 25); a rejected purge is
warned once.

Example:

```tsx
revalidatePath("/blog");
```

### revalidateTag

Function. `import { revalidateTag } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export function revalidateTag(tag: string): void;
```

Purges every cached ISR page tagged `tag` (`export const tags`), with the same timing and
reach as `revalidatePath`. Throws a TypeError for an invalid tag.

To purge every `nowaki start` instance, set `NOWAKI_REVALIDATE_SECRET` and send each one
`POST /__nowaki/revalidate` with `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` and a JSON body
`{ "paths": ["/blog"], "tags": ["posts"] }` (at most 256 entries). The endpoint is off (404)
while the variable is unset.

Example:

```tsx
revalidateTag(`post:${ctx.params.slug}`);
```

### getContext

Function. `import { getContext } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export function getContext(): LoaderContext | null;
```

While a server function (`"use server"`), a page `action`, an API route, or a live handler /
`live.authorize` is running, returns that call's LoaderContext (for live, the WebSocket
upgrade's cookie, authorization, accept-language, and user-agent headers). Returns null
elsewhere. Use it for auth.

Uses: [`LoaderContext`](#loadercontext).

### nonce

Function. `import { nonce } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export function nonce(): string;
```

The CSP nonce for an inline `<script>` or `<style>` the app renders on the server, under
`NOWAKI_CSP=report-only` / `enforce`. Put it in the tag's `nonce` attribute: the response's
nonce replaces it as the page is sent. Nowaki gives the nonce only to the tags it emits and to
tags carrying this value, so inline scripts and styles that reach the page as raw HTML
(`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, Markdown, a `head` string) don't run under `enforce`.

Call it while a request renders: in a page, layout, `meta()`, loader, action, middleware or
API route (including `ctx.html()`). Returns "" with `NOWAKI_CSP` off and outside a request.
A static `export const head` is evaluated once, so use `meta()` for a nonced tag there.
Static output (`nowaki prerender`) has no per-response nonce: "" there too.

Server-only (like `getContext`): don't import it in an island.

Examples:

```tsx
<style nonce={nonce()}>{css}</style>
```

```tsx
export const meta = () => ({ head: `<style nonce="${nonce()}">${css}</style>` });
```

### StandardSchemaV1

Interface. `import type { StandardSchemaV1 } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface StandardSchemaV1<Input = unknown, Output = Input> {
    readonly "~standard": {
        readonly version: 1;
        readonly vendor: string;
        readonly validate: (value: unknown) => StandardSchemaResult<Output> | Promise<StandardSchemaResult<Output>>;
        readonly types?: {
            readonly input: Input;
            readonly output: Output;
        };
    };
}
```

A [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) (zod, valibot, arktype, ...).

Members:

- `~standard`: The Standard Schema interface: `validate`, plus the input and output types.

Uses: [`StandardSchemaResult`](#standardschemaresult).

Used by: [`serverFn`](#serverfn), [`CollectionDefinition`](runtime-content.md#collectiondefinition), [`defineCollection`](runtime-content.md#definecollection), [`Shape`](runtime-env.md#shape).

### StandardSchemaResult

Type. `import type { StandardSchemaResult } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type StandardSchemaResult<Output> = {
    readonly value: Output;
    readonly issues?: undefined;
} | {
    readonly issues: ReadonlyArray<{
        readonly message: string;
        readonly path?: ReadonlyArray<PropertyKey | {
            readonly key: PropertyKey;
        }>;
    }>;
};
```

What a Standard Schema's `validate` returns: the value, or the issues.

Used by: [`StandardSchemaV1`](#standardschemav1).

### serverFn

Function. `import { serverFn } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export declare function serverFn<S extends StandardSchemaV1, R, Rest extends unknown[] = []>(schema: S, impl: (input: SchemaOutput<S>, ...rest: Rest) => R | Promise<R>): (input: SchemaInput<S>, ...rest: Rest) => Promise<Awaited<R>>;
```

A server function whose first argument is validated against `schema` before `impl` runs.
Invalid input is rejected with a 400 (`ServerFnError`, `data.issues`).

Example:

```tsx
export const addTodo = serverFn(z.string().min(1), async (text) => save(text));
```

Uses: [`StandardSchemaV1`](#standardschemav1), [`SchemaOutput`](#schemaoutput), [`SchemaInput`](#schemainput).

### ServerFnError

Class. `import { ServerFnError } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export declare class ServerFnError extends Error {
    constructor(message: string, options?: {
        status?: number;
        data?: unknown;
    });
    readonly status: number;
    readonly data?: unknown;
}
```

Throw from a server function to send `status` (default 400; a value outside 400-599 becomes 400)
and `message` (and `data`) to the client. `data` is sent as-is, so keep secrets out of it. Any
other error becomes a generic 500 in production.

Members:

- `constructor`: `message` is sent to the client as written, with `status` and `data`.
- `status`: The response status: `options.status` when it is 400-599, else 400.
- `data`: Extra data for the client (`options.data`), sent as-is.

### ViewTransition

Type. `import type { ViewTransition } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type ViewTransition = boolean;
```

`export const viewTransition = true` on a page route: client navigations to and from the page
run as View Transitions (`document.startViewTransition`), and full page loads between two such
pages get a cross-document one (`@view-transition { navigation: auto }`), also on pages that
ship no JS. Skipped when the browser lacks the API or the visitor prefers reduced motion. For a
single link, use `<Link viewTransition>` (or `data-nowaki-transition` on an `<a>`) instead, and
`transitionName()` from `@nowaki-dev/runtime/navigation` to morph an element into the next
page's. Off by default: a page without it gets nothing added to its HTML.

Example:

```tsx
export const viewTransition = true;
```

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule).

### Revalidate

Type. `import type { Revalidate } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type Revalidate = number;
```

`export const revalidate` on a page route: ISR. A render is cached for this many seconds (a
positive number) and re-rendered in the background once stale (`stale-while-revalidate`). Don't
put per-user data on such a page: Nowaki varies the cache by what the render read (cookies,
headers, the query), and a page that reads the session or cookies is never shared.

Example:

```tsx
export const revalidate = 60;
```

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule).

### PageScripts

Type. `import type { PageScripts } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export type PageScripts = readonly string[];
```

`export const scripts` on a page route or layout: modules shipped to the browser as
`<script type="module">`, bundled like an island but with no component and no hydration.
Read from the source at build time, so it must be an array of string literals: relative paths
(from the file that lists them) or package specifiers.

Example:

```tsx
export const scripts = ["./hero.ts"];
```

Used by: [`PageModule`](#pagemodule), [`LayoutModule`](#layoutmodule).

### PageModule

Interface. `import type { PageModule } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface PageModule<D = any> {
    default: (props: RouteProps<D>) => unknown;
    loader?: Loader<D>;
    action?: Action;
    meta?: Meta | MetaFn<D>;
    title?: string;
    head?: string;
    lang?: string;
    htmlAttrs?: DocumentAttrs;
    bodyAttrs?: DocumentAttrs;
    revalidate?: Revalidate;
    tags?: RouteTags;
    streaming?: Streaming;
    csrf?: Csrf;
    budget?: RouteBudget;
    viewTransition?: ViewTransition;
    staticPaths?: StaticPaths;
    prerender?: boolean;
    sitemap?: boolean;
    scripts?: PageScripts;
}
```

The exports a page route module (`routes/**/*.tsx`, also `_404` / `_500`) may have, with their
types. Check one export with an indexed type, or the whole module from another file:

Members:

- `default`: The page component.
- `loader`: See [`Loader`](#loader).
- `action`: Runs on every method but GET, HEAD and OPTIONS.
- `meta`: The page's metadata: an object, or a function of the loader data (see [`MetaFn`](#metafn)).
- `title`: `<title>`. `meta.title` wins over it.
- `head`: Raw HTML put in `<head>` as written (no escaping: never build it from user input).
- `lang`: `<html lang>`. With i18n it defaults to the request's locale.
- `htmlAttrs`: See [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs).
- `bodyAttrs`: See [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs).
- `revalidate`: See [`Revalidate`](#revalidate).
- `tags`: See [`RouteTags`](#routetags).
- `streaming`: See [`Streaming`](#streaming).
- `csrf`: See [`Csrf`](#csrf).
- `budget`: See [`RouteBudget`](#routebudget).
- `viewTransition`: See [`ViewTransition`](#viewtransition).
- `staticPaths`: See [`StaticPaths`](#staticpaths).
- `prerender`: `false` leaves the page out of `nowaki prerender` / the static adapter.
- `sitemap`: `false` leaves the page out of the generated sitemap.xml.
- `scripts`: See [`PageScripts`](#pagescripts).

Example:

```tsx
export const revalidate: PageModule["revalidate"] = 60;
export const meta = { title: "Blog" } satisfies PageModule["meta"];
// routes.check.ts
import * as blog from "./routes/blog.tsx";
blog satisfies PageModule;
```

Uses: [`RouteProps`](#routeprops), [`Loader`](#loader), [`Action`](#action), [`Meta`](#meta), [`MetaFn`](#metafn), [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs), [`Revalidate`](#revalidate), [`RouteTags`](#routetags), [`Streaming`](#streaming), [`Csrf`](#csrf), [`RouteBudget`](#routebudget), [`ViewTransition`](#viewtransition), [`StaticPaths`](#staticpaths), [`PageScripts`](#pagescripts).

### LayoutModule

Interface. `import type { LayoutModule } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime";`

```ts
export interface LayoutModule<D = any> {
    default: (props: LayoutProps<D>) => unknown;
    loader?: Loader<D>;
    meta?: Meta | MetaFn<D>;
    title?: string;
    head?: string;
    lang?: string;
    htmlAttrs?: DocumentAttrs;
    bodyAttrs?: DocumentAttrs;
    scripts?: PageScripts;
}
```

The exports a `_layout` module may have (a layout's `meta` applies to every page under it).

Members:

- `default`: The layout component.
- `loader`: See [`Loader`](#loader).
- `meta`: Defaults for every page under the layout: page values win, and `openGraph` and `twitter` merge
  one level deep. Only an object is read on a layout; a function is not called.
- `title`: Not read on a layout: set `meta.title`, the title of pages that have none of their own.
- `head`: Raw HTML added to the `<head>` of every page under the layout (root layout first, before the
  page's own `head`). No escaping: never build it from user input.
- `lang`: Not read on a layout: set `htmlAttrs.lang`, used by pages without their own `lang` (with
  i18n, the request's locale comes first).
- `htmlAttrs`: See [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs).
- `bodyAttrs`: See [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs).
- `scripts`: See [`PageScripts`](#pagescripts).

Uses: [`LayoutProps`](#layoutprops), [`Loader`](#loader), [`Meta`](#meta), [`MetaFn`](#metafn), [`DocumentAttrs`](#documentattrs), [`PageScripts`](#pagescripts).
